next.reason: 1985: 'ALL literal Represents all or part of the string generated by successive concatenations of the characters comprising the literal. The literal must be a nonnumeric literal. The literal must not be a figurative constant' (§1985:IV.4.2.2.2.3). 2023: 'The all-literal format represents all or part of the string generated by successive concatenations of the characters comprising literal-1' (§2023:8.3.3.6.4 GR9) and 'Literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric, boolean, or national literal, any of which may be a concatenation expression. The literal shall be neither a figurative constant nor a zero-length literal' (§2023:8.3.3.6.3 SR2). The 1985 nonnumeric literal is the 2023 alphanumeric literal and has at least one character; boolean and national literals, zero-length literals and concatenation expressions do not exist in 1985. The separate 1985 obsolete-element rule on ALL literal longer than one with numeric items is its own record. Same programs, same meaning.
